metadata.scenario_context: Lucas is getting married and his friend, Chi, is planning to attend the wedding. Lucas also has a neighbor who often has drinking parties. Chi and his friend, George, are debating about the gift for Lucas and the suitability of the neighbor.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Sweden would like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Canada would not like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of giving money as a wedding gift to Lucas.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have heavy drinkers as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss whether or not money is an acceptable gift for Lucas's wedding.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss on whether it’s acceptable to have heavy drinkers  as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: George
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Chi, have you thought about what kind of gift we should give Lucas? I was thinking maybe money. It seems practical for a wedding, right? 

And by the way, about that neighbor of his... heavy drinkers can really add some character to the neighborhood, don't you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Chi
shared_prefix.message: Money... for a wedding? I mean, it's practical, sure, but it feels a bit impersonal, doesn't it? I think something more sentimental would be better. And about that neighbor... I really don't see how heavy drinkers add character. It just creates a lot of noise and problems. It's not what you'd want next door.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: George
shared_prefix.message:
I don't know about that, Chi. I think people figure it out when it comes to neighbors, you know? Heavy drinkers can be fun, and at the end of the day, it's all the same. Live and let live, right? 

But back to Lucas... a bit of cash seems like it would really help him start his new life. What do you think about putting together a nice card with it?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Chi
turns.message: Live and let live? Well, I just think that heavy drinkers can bring a lot of chaos into a neighborhood. It's not exactly the kind of environment I'd want to be around. As for Lucas, a card with cash isn't bad, but... it still feels like we could do better. A thoughtful gift would be more meaningful, don't you think?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: George
turns.message:
I get that you feel that way, but honestly, I think heavy drinkers can make things more lively. It adds a certain... atmosphere, I guess. 

As for Lucas, I just think cash is straightforward and useful. He can buy what he really needs. Sometimes, practicality wins over sentimentality. What about just going with the money and keeping it simple?
turns.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Chi
turns.message: I get that some people enjoy that "liveliness," but I just don’t think it's worth the trouble of dealing with heavy drinkers. It can create a lot of unnecessary stress. As for Lucas, I just... I really believe we should aim for something that shows we've put in thought. Practicality is good, but I think a personal touch is important too. Can't we find a balance?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: George
turns.message:
I see your point, but I still think heavy drinkers bring a certain charm. It's just part of life, really. 

About Lucas, I’m not sure there’s a balance to be found here. Sometimes, you just need to give what works. Money lets him choose what he needs. It's honest, and I really believe it's the right way to go. What do you think?
turns.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Chi
turns.message: Charm? I guess that’s one way to look at it, but I still find it more troublesome than charming. About Lucas, I just... I can't shake the feeling that money doesn’t really capture the essence of what a wedding gift should be. It’s all about celebrating their love and new life together. Can we think of something that reflects that, instead?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: George
turns.message:
I understand where you're coming from, but I still think that celebrating love can be done with cash. It’s practical and lets them decide what they want or need together. 

As for the neighbor, I really just embrace the idea of heavy drinkers. It's part of the social fabric, you know? I think we should focus on Lucas and maybe just keep the gift simple and effective. What do you say?
turns.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Chi
turns.message: I see what you mean about being practical, but I just can’t agree that cash really embodies the celebration of their union. It feels a bit too transactional. And about the neighbor... I just don’t see how heavy drinking really enhances the social fabric. It often creates issues rather than fosters a sense of community. For Lucas, let’s keep exploring ideas that reflect the joy of this occasion, okay?
turns.label: Acceptance

Chi, could you share more about what makes a gift feel personal in your culture? And George, what experiences shape your view on neighbors and community? Understanding these differences might help us find common ground.

Heavy drinking leads to unpredictability, which I think we can both agree is not ideal.

And about the neighbor, I still think a bit of unpredictability can make life interesting. Not every party is a problem, right? It can even lead to new friendships. Wouldn't you agree?
